title: Structural isomers
keyIdea: Structural isomers have the same molecular formula but their atoms are bonded in a different order. Chain isomers have different carbon skeletons (butane and 2-methylpropane, both C₄H₁₀). Position isomers have the same group on a different carbon (propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol). Functional group isomers have different groups (ethanol and methoxymethane, both C₂H₆O). Bending or flipping a drawing does not make a new isomer.

kid: Isomers are like words made from the same letters. Stop and pots use the same four letters in a new order, so they are different words.

Butane has 4 carbon atoms and 10 hydrogen atoms. Its carbons sit in a row. Move one carbon so it joins the middle of the row. You still have 4 carbons and 10 hydrogens, but now it is a new compound called 2-methylpropane.
Bending a chain does not count. A chain can twist like a piece of string. If each atom is still joined to the same atoms as before, it is the same thing.
Isomers can act in different ways. Butane boils at about −1 °C. 2-methylpropane boils at about −12 °C. The branched one is more compact, so its molecules touch less and pull on each other less.
adult: Structural isomers have the same molecular formula, but their atoms are joined in a different order. Count both formulas first. If they differ, the two are not isomers, however alike they look. Butane and pentane differ by CH₂: they are members of one homologous series, not isomers.

There are three kinds. Chain isomers have different carbon chains. Pentane, 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane are the three isomers of C₅H₁₂. Position isomers keep the chain and the group but move the group, as in propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol. Functional group isomers have different groups: ethanol, an alcohol, and methoxymethane, an ether, are both C₂H₆O.

Isomers have different properties. Branching makes a molecule more compact. Compact molecules touch less, so the forces between them are weaker and the boiling point falls: pentane 36 °C, 2-methylbutane 28 °C, 2,2-dimethylpropane 10 °C. Ethanol boils at 78 °C but methoxymethane at −24 °C. The O–H in ethanol lets its molecules form hydrogen bonds.

Watch for common mistakes. A bent or flipped drawing is not a new isomer. 2-methylbutane is not 3-methylbutane: number from the end nearer the branch. 1-methylpropane is just butane drawn oddly. Propan-3-ol is propan-1-ol counted from the wrong end. Molecules with different formulas are never isomers.

familyTip: Use four coins as carbon atoms. Lay them in a row, then move one to touch the middle coin. Ask: is it a new shape, or just the row bent? Only a coin joined to a different coin makes a new isomer.

worked.title: Draw and name every alcohol with the formula C₄H₁₀O.
steps: Start with the straight four-carbon chain. –OH on carbon 1 gives butan-1-ol. –OH on carbon 2 gives butan-2-ol. Carbon 3 is carbon 2 counted from the other end, so it adds nothing new.
Now use the branched skeleton, 2-methylpropane. –OH on an end carbon gives 2-methylpropan-1-ol. All three end carbons are the same, so that is one isomer.
So there are 4 alcohols. With the 3 ethers (1-methoxypropane, 2-methoxypropane and ethoxyethane), C₄H₁₀O has 7 structural isomers. Check each has 4 C, 10 H and 1 O.

practice.prompt: An alkane has {n} carbon atoms. How many hydrogen atoms does each of its isomers have?
practice.hint: Isomers share one molecular formula. Alkanes are CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.
practice.explain: Every isomer has 2 × {n} + 2 = {=2*n+2} hydrogen atoms. Branching moves atoms; it never adds or removes any.

practice.hint: Write the molecular formula of each. Isomers need the same one.
practice.explain: Butane and 2-methylpropane are both C₄H₁₀ with different skeletons. Butane and pentane differ by CH₂, and ethane has no oxygen.

practice.prompt: What type of isomers are propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol?
practice.hint: Is the carbon chain different, or only where the –OH is?
practice.explain: Both have a straight three-carbon chain and an –OH. Only the carbon carrying the –OH changes, so they are position isomers.

practice.prompt: How many structural isomers does C₅H₁₂ have?
practice.hint: Try a straight chain, one branch, then two branches on one carbon.
practice.explain: Pentane, 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane. Other drawings are these bent, flipped or numbered from the wrong end.

practice.prompt: A chain of {n} carbon atoms has an –OH on carbon 2. Counted from the other end, which carbon is the –OH on?
practice.hint: Number the chain backwards: the last carbon becomes carbon 1.
practice.explain: From the other end it is carbon {=n-1}. Names use the end that gives the lower number, so the –OH is on carbon 2 either way.

pool.prompt: A student draws butane bent into an L and says it is a new isomer. Is she right?
choices: No: the atoms bond in the same order, so it is still butane
pool.hint: Follow the bonds from one end. Is each carbon joined to the same carbons as before?
pool.explain: The longest chain is still four carbons in a row. Chains twist freely, so it is butane. 1-methylpropane is not a real name: it is butane.

pool.prompt: Ethanol and methoxymethane are both C₂H₆O. What kind of isomers are they?
pool.hint: Ethanol has C–O–H. Where is the oxygen in methoxymethane?
pool.explain: Methoxymethane is C–O–C, an ether. Ethanol is an alcohol. Different functional groups make them functional group isomers.

pool.prompt: What is the correct name for CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₃?
pool.hint: Find the longest chain, then number from the end nearer the branch.
pool.explain: The longest chain has four carbons with a methyl on carbon 2 from the right-hand end: 2-methylbutane. 3-methylbutane numbers from the wrong end.

pool.prompt: An alcohol has {n} carbon atoms, one oxygen atom and only single bonds. How many hydrogen atoms does it have?
pool.hint: Alcohols are CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH. Add the H in the –OH.
pool.explain: 2 × {n} + 1 + 1 = {=2*n+2}. Its ether isomers have the same number.

pool.prompt: Which has the lowest boiling point?
pool.hint: More branching gives a more compact molecule with less surface contact.
pool.explain: 2,2-dimethylpropane boils at about 10 °C, 2-methylbutane at 28 °C and pentane at 36 °C. All three are C₅H₁₂.

pool.prompt: Why does ethanol boil at 78 °C but methoxymethane at −24 °C?
choices: Ethanol's O–H lets its molecules hydrogen bond to each other
Methoxymethane has a smaller molecular formula
pool.hint: They have exactly the same atoms. What bond does only ethanol have?
pool.explain: Both are C₂H₆O. Only ethanol has an O–H, so its molecules form hydrogen bonds, which take more energy to break.

choices: No, they are the same compound written from the other end
pool.explain: Both are propan-1-ol: the –OH is on an end carbon. Writing a formula backwards does not make a new compound.

pool.prompt: Are butane, C₄H₁₀, and pentane, C₅H₁₂, isomers?
choices: No: their molecular formulas are different
pool.hint: Isomers must share one molecular formula. Count the carbon and hydrogen atoms in each.
pool.explain: Isomers must have the same molecular formula. These differ by CH₂, so they are neighbours in the alkane series.

pool.prompt: How many structural isomers does C₆H₁₄ have?
pool.hint: Straight chain; one methyl on carbon 2 or 3; two methyls on one carbon or on neighbours.

pool.prompt: A straight chain of {n} carbon atoms has an –OH on carbon {=n-1}, counted from the left. What locant number belongs in its correct name?
pool.hint: Names number from the end that gives the –OH the lower number.
pool.explain: Counted from the right, carbon {=n-1} is carbon 2, which is lower. So the name has -2-ol, not -{=n-1}-ol.

pool.prompt: Which of these is NOT an isomer of C₄H₁₀O?
pool.hint: Count the carbon atoms in each name.
pool.explain: Propan-1-ol is C₃H₈O, with one carbon fewer. Butan-2-ol and ethoxyethane both have 4 C, 10 H and 1 O.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: move end atoms on a peg board and watch the name, formula and boiling point update, from butane to ethers.
